correctness.rationale: For a Hermitian hopping matrix the sink cyclic space and its orthogonal complement reduce H and the single-site damping. On the complement evolution is unitary. On the cyclic space an eigenvector of the damped generator with Re eigenvalue zero would have no sink component (take the real part of the Rayleigh quotient) and hence be an H eigenvector orthogonal to the whole cyclic space. Thus every generator eigenvalue on the cyclic space has strictly negative real part, which gives norm decay even without diagonalizability. Independently compute the cyclic space by scaling J out of H. Let δ=w−1, A'=a₁+r_A, B'=b₀+r_B. H a₁=B′ and H²a₁=(n+δ)a₀+nA′; H³a₁=[n(m−1)+(n+δ)]B′+δ(n+δ)b₀. For w>0, w≠1, δ(n+δ)≠0, so b₀ and r_B are cyclic. H b₀ and H r_B/(n−1) differ by δa₀, so a₀, A′ and hence r_A are cyclic. Conversely the five orbit sums form an invariant subspace; all five are orthogonal and nonzero under m,n≥3. At w=1 the first three powers span a₁, the uniform A vector and the uniform B vector, which close under H, so the rank is three. Orthogonal projection onto the orbit sums gives the displayed diagonal captures; trace divided by m+n gives the maximally mixed result. Taking t→∞ at fixed defect is essential; finite-time norm is continuous in w.
residual_risks: Only one nonincident positive real hopping defect, one absorber with κ>0, and no dephasing. The limit says nothing about defect-dependent decay rates or additional defect/sink configurations.

The six-site complete-graph perturbation of Bassereh et al. varies a bond incident to the trap and reports enhancement or perfect transfer. The same orbit argument for that example gives a three-dimensional defective cyclic space instead of a five-dimensional bipartite one.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A rank-one theorem with richer dephasing hypotheses does not dominate the noiseless rank-two defect. The complete-graph example cannot be specialized to this cross-part defect on a bipartite graph with a nonincident absorber.

value.rationale: For a natural perturbation of a standard coherent network, the result does more than show generic enhancement: it rules out exceptional permitted nonzero defects, determines which exact components become capturable, and quantifies a discontinuous infinite-time observable despite continuous finite-time evolution. It gives exact sitewise predictions even for starts away from the trap or defective edge, which a rank count or the known unweighted law cannot provide.
residual_risks: No assertion of benefit at finite time, robustness under noise, or a thermodynamic transition.
